```json
      "title": "Stream Type",
      "default": "all",
      "description": "Defines the type of events that are returned * `all` returns everything for a user and is the default * `changes` returns events that may cause file tree changes   such as file updates or collaborations. * `sync` is similar to `changes` but only applies to synced folders * `admin_logs` returns all events for an entire enterprise and   requires the user making the API call to have admin permissions. This   stream type is for programmatically pulling from a 1 year history of   events across all users within the enterprise and within a   `created_after` and `created_before` time frame. The complete history   of events will be returned in chronological order based on the event   time, but latency will be much higher than `admin_logs_streaming`. * `admin_logs_streaming` returns all events for an entire enterprise and   requires the user making the API call to have admin permissions. This   stream type is for polling for recent events across all users within   the enterprise. Latency will be much lower than `admin_logs`, but   events will not be returned in chronological order and may   contain duplicates. "
```

## BOX_LIST_FILE_APP_ITEM_ASSOCIATIONS
**This is a beta feature, which means that its availability might be limited.** Returns all app items the file is associated with. This includes app items associated with ancestors of the file. Assuming the context user has access to the file, the type/ids are revealed even if the context user does not have **View** permission on the app item.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListFileAppItemAssociationsRequest",
  "required": [
    "file_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "limit": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Limit",
      "description": "The maximum number of items to return per page. Default is 10, maximum is 100."
    },
    "marker": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Marker",
      "description": "Defines the position marker at which to begin returning results. This is used when paginating using marker-based pagination. Use the `next_marker` value from a previous response to get the next page of results."
    },
    "file_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "File Id",
      "description": "The unique identifier that represents a file. The ID for any file can be determined by visiting a file in the web application and copying the ID from the URL. For example, for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/files/123` the `file_id` is `123`."
    },
    "application_type": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Application Type",
      "description": "If specified, only return app items for this application type. Example values include 'hubs' for Box Hubs associations."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request schema for `ListFileAppItemAssociations`"
}
```

## BOX_LIST_FILE_COLLABORATIONS
Retrieves a list of pending and active collaborations for a file. This returns all the users that have access to the file or have been invited to the file.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListFileCollaborationsRequest",
  "required": [
    "file_id"
  ],
  "properties": {

    },
    "fields": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Fields",
      "description": "A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the response. This can be used to request fields that are not normally returned in a standard response. Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the effect that none of the standard fields are returned in the response unless explicitly specified, instead only fields for the mini representation are returned, additional to the fields requested. "
    },
    "marker": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Marker",
      "description": "Defines the position marker at which to begin returning results. This is used when paginating using marker-based pagination. Use the 'next_marker' value from a previous response to retrieve the next page of results."
    },
    "file_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "File Id",
      "description": "The unique identifier that represents a file. The ID for any file can be determined by visiting a file in the web application and copying the ID from the URL. For example, for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/files/123` the `file_id` is `123`. "
    }
  },
  "description": "Request schema for `ListFileCollaborations`"
}
```

## BOX_LIST_FILES_ON_LEGAL_HOLD_POLICY_ASSIGNMENT
Get a list of files with current file versions for a legal hold assignment. In some cases you may want to get previous file versions instead. In these cases, use the `GET /legal_hold_policy_assignments/:id/file_versions_on_hold` API instead to return any previous versions of a file for this legal hold policy assignment. Due to ongoing re-architecture efforts this API might not return all file versions held for this policy ID. Instead, this API will only return the latest file version held in the newly developed architecture. The `GET /file_version_legal_holds` API can be used to fetch current and past versions of files held within the legacy architecture. This endpoint does not support returning any content that is on hold due to a Custodian collaborating on a Hub. The `GET /legal_hold_policy_assignments?policy_id={id}` API can be used to find a list of policy assignments for a given policy ID.

**Input schema:**
```json

    "legal_hold_policy_assignment_id"

        "type": "string"
      },

Common fields include: id, type, name, sha1, file_version. Note: Specifying fields returns only mini representation plus the requested fields."
    },
    "marker": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Marker",
      "description": "Cursor position for marker-based pagination. Use the 'next_marker' value from a previous response to retrieve the next page of results."
    },
    "legal_hold_policy_assignment_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Legal Hold Policy Assignment Id",
      "description": "The unique identifier of the legal hold policy assignment. Obtain this ID by listing assignments for a legal hold policy using the 'List legal hold policy assignments' action with a policy_id."

}
```

## BOX_LIST_FILE_VERSION_LEGAL_HOLDS
Get a list of file versions on legal hold for a legal hold assignment. Due to ongoing re-architecture efforts this API might not return all file versions for this policy ID. Instead, this API will only return file versions held in the legacy architecture. Two new endpoints will available to request any file versions held in the new architecture. For file versions held in the new architecture, the `GET /legal_hold_policy_assignments/:id/file_versions_on_hold` API can be used to return all past file versions available for this policy assignment, and the `GET /legal_hold_policy_assignments/:id/files_on_hold` API can be used to return any current (latest) versions of a file under legal hold. The `GET /legal_hold_policy_assignments?policy_id={id}` API can be used to find a list of policy assignments for a given policy ID. Once the re-architecture is completed this API will be deprecated.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListFileVersionLegalHoldsRequest",
  "required": [
    "policy_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "limit": {

      "title": "Limit",

    },
    "marker": {

      "title": "Policy Id",
      "description": "The unique identifier (ID) of the legal hold policy. Use BOX_LIST_ALL_LEGAL_HOLD_POLICIES to retrieve available policy IDs."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request schema for `ListFileVersionLegalHolds`"
}
```

## BOX_LIST_FILE_VERSION_RETENTIONS
Retrieves all file version retentions for the given enterprise. **Note**: File retention API is now **deprecated**. To get information about files and file versions under retention, see [files under retention](e://get-retention-policy-assignments-id-files-under-retention) or [file versions under retention](e://get-retention-policy-assignments-id-file-versions-under-retention) endpoints.

## BOX_LIST_FOLDER_APP_ITEM_ASSOCIATIONS
**This is a beta feature, which means that its availability might be limited.** Returns all app items the folder is associated with. This includes app items associated with ancestors of the folder. Assuming the context user has access to the folder, the type/ids are revealed even if the context user does not have **View** permission on the app item.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListFolderAppItemAssociationsRequest",
  "required": [
    "folder_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "limit": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Limit",
      "description": "The maximum number of items to return per page. Maximum value is 1000."
    },
    "marker": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Marker",
      "description": "Defines the position marker at which to begin returning results. This is used when paginating using marker-based pagination. The value should be taken from the `next_marker` field returned in a previous response."
    },
    "folder_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Folder Id",
      "description": "The unique identifier that represent a folder. The ID for any folder can be determined by visiting this folder in the web application and copying the ID from the URL. For example, for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/folder/123` the `folder_id` is `123`. The root folder of a Box account is always represented by the ID `0`. "
    },
    "application_type": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Application Type",
      "description": "If given, returns only app items for this application type. Example values include 'hubs' for Box Hubs associations."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request schema for `ListFolderAppItemAssociations`"
}
```

## BOX_LIST_FOLDER_COLLABORATIONS
Retrieves a list of pending and active collaborations for a folder. This returns all the users that have access to the folder or have been invited to the folder.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListFolderCollaborationsRequest",
  "required": [
    "folder_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "limit": {

Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the effect that none of the standard fields are returned in the response unless explicitly specified, instead only fields for the mini representation are returned, additional to the fields requested. "
    },
    "marker": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Marker",
      "description": "Defines the position marker at which to begin returning results. This is used when paginating using marker-based pagination to retrieve the next page of results. "
    },
    "folder_id": {

      "title": "Folder Id",

    }
  },
  "description": "Request schema for `ListFolderCollaborations`"
}
```

## BOX_LIST_GROUP_COLLABORATIONS
Retrieves all the collaborations for a group. The user must have admin permissions to inspect enterprise's groups. Each collaboration object has details on which files or folders the group has access to and with what role.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListGroupCollaborationsRequest",
  "required": [
    "group_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "limit": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Limit",
      "description": "The maximum number of items to return per page. Default is 100, maximum is 1000."
    },
    "offset": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Offset",
      "default": 0,
      "description": "The offset of the item at which to begin the response. Use for pagination. Queries with offset parameter value exceeding 10000 will be rejected with a 400 response."
    },
    "group_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Group Id",
      "description": "The unique identifier of the group. Use the 'List groups for enterprise' action to retrieve available group IDs."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request schema for `ListGroupCollaborations`"
}
```

## BOX_LIST_HOLD_FILE_VERSIONS
Retrieves a list of previous (non-current) file versions that are on legal hold for a specific legal hold policy assignment. This endpoint returns file versions held under the new Box architecture. For current (latest) file versions, use BOX_REVIEW_FILES_ON_LEGAL_HOLD_POLICY_ASSIGNMENT instead. For file versions in the legacy architecture, use BOX_LIST_FILE_VERSION_LEGAL_HOLDS. Note: Due to ongoing re-architecture efforts, this API might not return all file versions held for this policy ID. This endpoint does not support returning content that is on hold due to a Custodian collaborating on a Hub. Requires the 'manage_legal_holds' scope and Legal Hold feature enabled for the enterprise.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",

    "legal_hold_policy_assignment_id"
  ],

      "title": "Limit",

      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Fields",
      "description": "A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the response. Use this to request specific fields like 'id', 'sha1', 'name', 'size', etc. If specified, only the requested fields plus mini representation fields are returned."
    },
    "marker": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Marker",
      "description": "The position marker for pagination. Use the 'next_marker' value from a previous response to retrieve the next page of results."
    },
    "legal_hold_policy_assignment_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Legal Hold Policy Assignment Id",
      "description": "The unique identifier (ID) of the legal hold policy assignment. This ID is returned when creating an assignment via BOX_ASSIGN_LEGAL_HOLD_POLICY or can be obtained by listing assignments with BOX_LIST_LEGAL_HOLD_POLICY_ASSIGNMENTS."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request schema for `ListHoldFileVersions`"
}
```

## BOX_LIST_ITEMS_IN_FOLDER
Retrieves a page of items in a folder. These items can be files, folders, and web links. To request more information about the folder itself, like its size, use the [Get a folder](#get-folders-id) endpoint instead.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListItemsInFolderRequest",
  "required": [
    "folder_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "sort": {
      "enum": [
        "date",
        "id",
        "name",
        "size"
      ],
      "type": "string",
      "title": "SortEnm0",
      "description": "Defines the **second** attribute by which items are sorted. The folder type affects the way the items are sorted:   * **Standard folder**:   Items are always sorted by   their `type` first, with   folders listed before files,   and files listed   before web links.   * **Root folder**:   This parameter is not supported   for marker-based pagination   on the root folder   (the folder with an `id` of `0`).   * **Shared folder with parent path   to the associated folder visible to   the collaborator**:   Items are always sorted by   their `type` first, with   folders listed before files,   and files listed   before web links. "
    },
    "limit": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Limit",
      "description": "The maximum number of items to return per page."
    },
    "fields": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Fields",
      "description": "A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the response. This can be used to request fields that are not normally returned in a standard response. Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the effect that none of the standard fields are returned in the response unless explicitly specified, instead only fields for the mini representation are returned, additional to the fields requested. Additionally this field can be used to query any metadata applied to the file by specifying the `metadata` field as well as the scope and key of the template to retrieve, for example `?fields=metadata.enterprise_12345.contractTemplate`. "
    },
    "marker": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Marker",
      "description": "Defines the position marker at which to begin returning results. This is used when paginating using marker-based pagination. This requires `usemarker` to be set to `true`. "
    },
    "offset": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Offset",
      "default": 0,
      "description": "The offset of the item at which to begin the response. Queries with offset parameter value exceeding 10000 will be rejected with a 400 response. "
    },
    "direction": {
      "enum": [
        "ASC",
        "DESC"
      ],
      "type": "string",
      "title": "DirectionEnm0",
      "description": "The direction to sort results in. This can be either in alphabetical ascending (`ASC`) or descending (`DESC`) order. "
    },
    "folder_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Folder Id",
      "description": "The unique identifier that represent a folder. The ID for any folder can be determined by visiting this folder in the web application and copying the ID from the URL. For example, for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/folder/123` the `folder_id` is `123`. The root folder of a Box account is always represented by the ID `0`. "
    },
    "usemarker": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Usemarker",
      "description": "Specifies whether to use marker-based pagination instead of offset-based pagination. Only one pagination method can be used at a time. By setting this value to true, the API will return a `marker` field that can be passed as a parameter to this endpoint to get the next page of the response. "
    }
  },
  "description": "Request schema for `ListItemsInFolder`"
}
```

## BOX_LIST_METADATA_TAXONOMY_NODES
Retrieves metadata taxonomy nodes based on the specified parameters. Use when you need to browse or search hierarchical metadata classifications in Box. Results are sorted in lexicographic order unless a query parameter is passed, in which case results are sorted by relevance.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListMetadataTaxonomyNodesRequest",
  "required": [
    "namespace",
    "taxonomy_key"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "level": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "integer"
      },
      "title": "Level",
      "examples": [
        [
          1
        ]
      ],
      "description": "Filters results by taxonomy level. Multiple values can be provided. Results include nodes that match any of the specified values."
    },
    "limit": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Limit",
      "examples": [
        1000
      ],
      "description": "The maximum number of items to return per page."
    },
    "query": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Query",
      "examples": [
        "France"
      ],
      "description": "Query text to search for the taxonomy nodes. When specified, results are sorted by relevance instead of lexicographic order."
    },
    "marker": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Marker",
      "examples": [
        "JV9IRGZmieiBasejOG9yDCRNgd2ymoZIbjsxbJMjIs3kioVii"
      ],
      "description": "Defines the position marker at which to begin returning results. This is used when paginating using marker-based pagination. This requires usemarker to be set to true."
    },
    "parent": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Parent",
      "examples": [
        [
          "c73a9bf3-f377-4210-9159-3df06a481905"
        ]
      ],
      "description": "Node identifier of a direct parent node. Multiple values can be provided. Results include nodes that match any of the specified values."
    },
    "ancestor": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Ancestor",
      "examples": [
        [
          "c73a9bf3-f377-4210-9159-3df06a481905",
          "bf8b8213-be1f-4011-bd45-533c0713fa0a"
        ]
      ],
      "description": "Node identifier of any ancestor node. Multiple values can be provided. Results include nodes that match any of the specified values."
    },
    "namespace": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Namespace",
      "examples": [
        "enterprise_123456"
      ],
      "description": "The namespace of the metadata taxonomy. Typically starts with 'enterprise_' followed by your enterprise ID."
    },
    "taxonomy_key": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Taxonomy Key",
      "examples": [
        "geography"
      ],
      "description": "The key of the metadata taxonomy. This is the unique identifier for the taxonomy template."
    },
    "include-total-result-count": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Include Total Result Count",
      "description": "When set to true, provides the total number of nodes that matched the query. The response will compute counts of up to 10,000 elements. Defaults to false."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request schema for `ListMetadataTaxonomyNodes`"
}
```

## BOX_LIST_PENDING_COLLABORATIONS
Retrieves all pending collaboration invites for this user.

**Input schema:**
```json

    },

      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Fields",

Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the effect that none of the standard fields are returned in the response unless explicitly specified, instead only fields for the mini representation are returned, additional to the fields requested. Common fields include: id, type, status, role, created_at, modified_at, expires_at, invite_email, accessible_by, item."
    },
    "offset": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Offset",
      "default": 0,

    "status": {
      "enum": [

      ],

      "default": "pending",
      "description": "The status of the collaborations to retrieve. Must be 'pending'."
    }
  },

}
```

## BOX_LIST_RECENTLY_ACCESSED_ITEMS
Returns information about the recent items accessed by a user, either in the last 90 days or up to the last 1000 items accessed.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListRecentlyAccessedItemsRequest",
  "properties": {
    "limit": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Limit",
      "description": "The maximum number of items to return per page."
    },
    "fields": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Fields",
      "description": "A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the response. This can be used to request fields that are not normally returned in a standard response. Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the effect that none of the standard fields are returned in the response unless explicitly specified, instead only fields for the mini representation are returned, additional to the fields requested. "
    },
    "marker": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Marker",
      "description": "Defines the position marker at which to begin returning results. This is used when paginating using marker-based pagination. This requires `usemarker` to be set to `true`. "
    }
  },
  "description": "Request schema for `ListRecentlyAccessedItems`"
}
```

## BOX_LIST_RETENTION_POLICIES
Retrieves all of the retention policies for an enterprise.

**Input schema:**

## BOX_LIST_RETENTION_POLICY_ASSIGNMENTS
Retrieves all retention policy assignments for a specified retention policy. Retention policies can be assigned to: - 'enterprise': Apply to all content in the enterprise - 'folder': Apply to a specific folder - 'metadata_template': Apply based on metadata template values Requires the 'manage_retention_policies' scope.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListRetentionPolicyAssignmentsRequest",
  "required": [
    "retention_policy_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "type": {
      "enum": [
        "enterprise",
        "folder",
        "metadata_template"
      ],
      "type": "string",
      "title": "TypeEnm0",
      "description": "The type of retention policy assignment to filter by."
    },
    "limit": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Limit",
      "description": "Maximum number of assignments to return per page. Maximum value is 1000."
    },
    "fields": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Fields",
      "description": "A comma-separated list of additional fields to include in the response. Useful for requesting fields not returned by default. When specified, only mini representation fields plus the requested fields are returned."
    },
    "marker": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Marker",
      "description": "Pagination marker from a previous response's 'next_marker' field. Used to fetch the next page of results."
    },
    "retention_policy_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Retention Policy Id",
      "description": "The unique identifier of the retention policy to list assignments for. This ID can be obtained from the list retention policies endpoint."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request schema for `ListRetentionPolicyAssignments`"
}
```

## BOX_LIST_SHIELD_INFORMATION_BARRIER_REPORTS
Lists shield information barrier reports for a specified barrier. Shield information barrier reports contain details about barrier violations and compliance status. This feature requires Box Shield enterprise license. Returns a paginated list of report objects with status (pending/completed), creation timestamps, and details about the barrier scope.

## BOX_LIST_SHIELD_INFORMATION_BARRIER_SEGMENT_RESTRICTIONS
Lists all shield information barrier segment restrictions for a specific segment. Shield information barrier segment restrictions define which segments are prevented from collaborating with each other. This endpoint retrieves all restrictions where the specified segment is the requesting segment (the segment whose members are restricted from collaborating with other segments). Note: This feature requires Box Shield add-on and enterprise admin privileges. Returns 404 if Shield is not enabled for your enterprise or if the segment ID does not exist. Use Cases: - View all collaboration restrictions for a specific segment - Audit compliance boundaries between organizational divisions - Paginate through large sets of restrictions using marker-based pagination

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListShieldInformationBarrierSegmentRestrictionsRequest",
  "required": [
    "shield_information_barrier_segment_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "limit": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Limit",
      "description": "Maximum number of restriction items to return per page. Valid range is 1-1000. If not specified, the API uses its default page size."
    },
    "marker": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Marker",
      "description": "Pagination marker from a previous response's 'next_marker' field. Used to retrieve the next page of results when paginating through large result sets."
    },
    "shield_information_barrier_segment_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Shield Information Barrier Segment Id",
      "description": "The unique identifier of the shield information barrier segment to list restrictions for. Obtain this ID from the list_shield_information_barrier_segments or create_shield_information_barrier_segment actions."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request schema for `ListShieldInformationBarrierSegmentRestrictions`"
}
```

## BOX_LIST_SHIELD_INFORMATION_BARRIER_SEGMENTS
Retrieves a list of shield information barrier segment objects for the specified Information Barrier ID. Shield Information Barriers are used to separate individuals/groups within the same enterprise to prevent confidential information from passing between them. Segments define the groups of users that are separated by the barrier. Note: This is an enterprise-level feature that requires Box Shield to be enabled. Returns a 404 error if Shield Information Barriers is not available for the enterprise.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListShieldInformationBarrierSegmentsRequest",
  "required": [
    "shield_information_barrier_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "limit": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Limit",
      "description": "The maximum number of items to return per page. Maximum value is 1000."
    },
    "marker": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Marker",
      "description": "Defines the position marker at which to begin returning results. This is used when paginating using marker-based pagination. Use the next_marker value from a previous response to fetch the next page of results."
    },
    "shield_information_barrier_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Shield Information Barrier Id",
      "description": "The ID of the shield information barrier to retrieve segments for. This is a required parameter obtained from list or create shield information barrier actions."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request schema for `ListShieldInformationBarrierSegments`"
}
```

## BOX_LIST_SLACK_INTEGRATION_MAPPINGS

## BOX_LIST_TASK_ASSIGNMENTS
Lists all of the assignments for a given task. Returns a collection of task assignment objects showing who has been assigned to complete or review a task. Each assignment includes the assigned user's details, the assignment status, and the associated file information. This endpoint does not support pagination as tasks typically have a limited number of assignees.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListTaskAssignmentsRequest",

  "properties": {

      "type": "string",
      "title": "Task Id",
      "description": "The unique identifier of the task to retrieve assignments for. Task IDs can be obtained from the 'create_task' or 'list_tasks_on_file' actions. Example: '39641675308'."

  },
```

## BOX_LIST_TASKS_ON_FILE
Retrieves a list of all the tasks for a file. This endpoint does not support pagination.

**Input schema:**

## BOX_LIST_TEAMS_INTEGRATION_MAPPINGS
Lists [Teams integration mappings](https://support.box.com/hc/en-us/articles/360044681474-Using-Box-for-Teams) in a users' enterprise. You need Admin or Co-Admin role to use this endpoint.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListTeamsIntegrationMappingsRequest",
  "properties": {
    "box_item_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Box Item Id",
      "description": "Box item ID, for which the mappings should be returned"
    },
    "box_item_type": {
      "enum": [
        "folder"
      ],
      "type": "string",
      "title": "BoxItemTypeEnm0",
      "description": "Box item type, for which the mappings should be returned"
    },
    "partner_item_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Partner Item Id",
      "description": "ID of the mapped item, for which the mapping should be returned"
    },
    "partner_item_type": {
      "enum": [
        "channel",
        "team"
      ],
      "type": "string",
      "title": "PartnerItemTypeEnm0",
      "description": "Mapped item type, for which the mapping should be returned"
    }
  },
  "description": "Request schema for `ListTeamsIntegrationMappings`"
}
```

## BOX_LIST_TERMS_OF_SERVICE_USER_STATUSES
Retrieves a list of users and their acceptance status for a specific terms of service. Returns information about whether each user has accepted the terms, including: - User details (ID, name, email) - Acceptance status (accepted or not) - Creation and modification timestamps Note: This endpoint requires the Terms of Service feature to be enabled for the enterprise and appropriate admin permissions (manage enterprise properties or manage users). Use 'list_terms_of_services' first to get valid terms of service IDs.

```json
{
  "type": "object",

  "required": [
    "tos_id"

  "properties": {
    "tos_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Tos Id",
      "description": "The unique identifier of the terms of service to retrieve user statuses for. Use 'list_terms_of_services' action to find available terms of service IDs for your enterprise."
    },
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "description": "Optional. Filters results to show only the status for a specific user. If not provided, returns statuses for all users associated with the terms of service."
    }
  },

}
```

## BOX_LIST_TRASHED_ITEMS
Retrieves the files and folders that have been moved to the trash. Any attribute in the full files or folders objects can be passed in with the `fields` parameter to retrieve those specific attributes that are not returned by default. This endpoint defaults to use offset-based pagination, yet also supports marker-based pagination using the `marker` parameter.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListTrashedItemsRequest",
  "properties": {
    "sort": {
      "enum": [
        "date",
        "name",
        "size"
      ],
      "type": "string",
      "title": "SortEnm0",
      "description": "Defines the **second** attribute by which items are sorted. Items are always sorted by their `type` first, with folders listed before files, and files listed before web links. This parameter is not supported when using marker-based pagination. "
    },
    "limit": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Limit",
      "description": "The maximum number of items to return per page."
    },
    "fields": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Fields",
      "description": "A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the response. This can be used to request fields that are not normally returned in a standard response. Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the effect that none of the standard fields are returned in the response unless explicitly specified, instead only fields for the mini representation are returned, additional to the fields requested. "
    },
    "marker": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Marker",
      "description": "Defines the position marker at which to begin returning results. This is used when paginating using marker-based pagination. This requires `usemarker` to be set to `true`. "
    },
    "offset": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Offset",
      "default": 0,
      "description": "The offset of the item at which to begin the response. Queries with offset parameter value exceeding 10000 will be rejected with a 400 response. "
    },
    "direction": {
      "enum": [
        "ASC",
        "DESC"
      ],
      "type": "string",
      "title": "DirectionEnm0",
      "description": "The direction to sort results in. This can be either in alphabetical ascending (`ASC`) or descending (`DESC`) order. "
    },
    "usemarker": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Usemarker",
      "description": "Specifies whether to use marker-based pagination instead of offset-based pagination. Only one pagination method can be used at a time. By setting this value to true, the API will return a `marker` field that can be passed as a parameter to this endpoint to get the next page of the response. "
    }
  },
  "description": "Request schema for `ListTrashedItems`"
}
```

## BOX_LIST_UPLOAD_SESSION_PARTS
List the parts (chunks) that have been uploaded to a chunked upload session. This is useful for tracking upload progress, verifying which parts have been successfully uploaded, and determining which parts still need to be uploaded. The upload_session_id is obtained from the 'Create upload session' action. Note: Chunked uploads are only for files larger than 20MB.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListUploadSessionPartsRequest",
  "required": [
    "upload_session_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "limit": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Limit",
      "description": "The maximum number of parts to return per page. Maximum allowed value is 1000. If not specified, the server default is used."
    },
    "offset": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Offset",
      "default": 0,
      "description": "The zero-based offset of the first part to return. Used for pagination. Default is 0. Note: Queries with offset exceeding 10000 will be rejected with a 400 response."
    },
    "upload_session_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Upload Session Id",
      "description": "The unique identifier of the chunked upload session. This ID is returned when creating an upload session via the 'Create upload session' endpoint."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request schema for `ListUploadSessionParts`"
}
```

## BOX_LIST_USERS_EXEMPT_FROM_COLLABORATION_DOMAIN_RESTRICTIONS
Returns a list of users who have been exempt from the collaboration domain restrictions. Note: This endpoint requires an enterprise account with collaboration domain restrictions enabled. A 403 Forbidden error will be returned if the feature is not available for the enterprise.

## BOX_LIST_WEBHOOKS
Returns all defined webhooks for the requesting application. This API only returns webhooks that are applied to files or folders that are owned by the authenticated user. This means that an admin can not see webhooks created by a service account unless the admin has access to those folders, and vice versa.

```json
    "marker": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Marker",
      "description": "Pagination marker from a previous response's 'next_marker' field. Use this to retrieve the next page of results when paginating through webhooks."

}
```

## BOX_LIST_WORKFLOWS
Lists Box Relay workflows configured for a specific folder. Use the 'trigger_type' parameter to filter workflows by trigger type (e.g., 'WORKFLOW_MANUAL_START' for workflows that can be manually started via API). Your application must be authorized to use the 'Manage Box Relay' application scope within the Box developer console. Returns a paginated list of workflow objects with their flows and outcomes.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListWorkflowsRequest",
  "required": [
    "folder_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "limit": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Limit",
      "description": "The maximum number of workflows to return per page. If not specified, the API uses a default page size (typically 20). Maximum value varies by API."
    },
    "marker": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Marker",
      "description": "Defines the position marker at which to begin returning results. Used for cursor-based pagination. Obtain this value from the 'next_marker' field in a previous response to fetch the next page of results."
    },
    "folder_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Folder Id",
      "description": "The unique identifier of the folder to list workflows for. The ID for any folder can be determined by visiting this folder in the web application and copying the ID from the URL. For example, for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/folder/123` the `folder_id` is `123`. The root folder of a Box account is always represented by the ID `0`."
    },
    "trigger_type": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Trigger Type",
      "description": "Type of trigger to filter workflows by. Use 'WORKFLOW_MANUAL_START' to find workflows that can be manually triggered via the API."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request schema for `ListWorkflows`"
}
```

## BOX_PREFLIGHT_CHECK_BEFORE_UPLOAD
Performs a preflight check to verify that a file will be accepted by Box before uploading the entire file. This helps verify permissions, quota, and filename conflicts before starting the actual upload. A successful response (HTTP 200) indicates the upload can proceed. A 409 Conflict response indicates a file with the same name already exists.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "PreflightCheckBeforeUploadRequest",
  "required": [
    "name"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "name": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Name",
      "description": "The name for the file to be uploaded. Must be unique within the target folder."
    },
    "size": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Size",
      "description": "The size of the file in bytes. Used to verify storage quota availability."
    },
    "parent_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Parent Id",
      "default": "0",
      "description": "The ID of the parent folder where the file will be uploaded. Use '0' for the root folder."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request schema for `PreflightCheckBeforeUpload`"
}
```

## BOX_PROMOTE_FILE_VERSION
Promote a specific version of a file. If previous versions exist, this method can be used to promote one of the older versions to the top of the version history. This creates a new copy of the old version and puts it at the top of the versions history. The file will have the exact same contents as the older version, with the the same hash digest, `etag`, and name as the original. Other properties such as comments do not get updated to their former values. Don't use this endpoint to restore Box Notes, as it works with file formats such as PDF, DOC, PPTX or similar.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "PromoteFileVersionRequest",
  "required": [
    "file_id",
    "id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Id",
      "description": "The ID of the file version to promote to the current version. You can get file version IDs by calling the 'list_all_file_versions' action with the file_id. This creates a new copy of the specified version at the top of the version history."
    },
    "type": {
      "enum": [
        "file_version"
      ],
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Type",
      "default": "file_version",
      "description": "The type of item being promoted. Must be 'file_version'. Defaults to 'file_version' if not specified."
    },
    "fields": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Fields",
      "description": "A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the response. This can be used to request fields that are not normally returned in a standard response. Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the effect that none of the standard fields are returned in the response unless explicitly specified, instead only fields for the mini representation are returned, additional to the fields requested. "
    },
    "file_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "File Id",
      "description": "The unique identifier that represents a file. The ID for any file can be determined by visiting a file in the web application and copying the ID from the URL. For example, for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/files/123` the `file_id` is `123`. "
    }
  },
  "description": "Request schema for `PromoteFileVersion`"
}
```

## BOX_QUERY_FILES_FOLDERS_BY_METADATA
Query files and folders by metadata using SQL-like syntax. Returns items that have metadata instances matching the specified template and optional query conditions. Use this action when you need to find files/folders based on their metadata values rather than searching by file name or content. This is useful for locating documents based on custom attributes like status, category, department, dates, etc. Examples: - Find all files with a specific metadata template: set `from_` to "enterprise_XXXXX.templateKey" - Find files in a specific folder: set `ancestor_folder_id` to the folder ID (use "0" for all folders) - Filter by metadata values: use `query` and `query_params` (e.g., query="status = :val", query_params={"val": "approved"}) Note: Classification templates cannot be queried with this endpoint.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "QueryFilesFoldersByMetadataRequest",
  "required": [
    "from",
    "ancestor_folder_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "from": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "From",
      "description": "The metadata template to query. Must be in the form 'scope.templateKey'. For enterprise templates, use 'enterprise_XXXXX.templateKey' where XXXXX is your enterprise ID. For example: 'enterprise_1351007304.contractTemplate'. Note: Box-provided classification templates cannot be used with this endpoint. Use BOX_LIST_ALL_METADATA_TEMPLATES_FOR_ENTERPRISE to find available templates."
    },
    "limit": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Limit",
      "default": 100,
      "description": "A value between 0 and 100 that indicates the maximum number of results to return for a single request. This only specifies a maximum boundary and will not guarantee the minimum number of results returned. "
    },
    "query": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Query",
      "description": "Optional SQL-like filter expression to match metadata field values. Use parameterized values with ':' prefix (e.g., ':value') that map to query_params. Examples: 'status = :val', 'amount >= :min AND amount <= :max', 'category LIKE :pattern'. Supported operators: =, <, >, <=, >=, <>, LIKE, NOT LIKE, ILIKE, NOT ILIKE, IS NULL, IS NOT NULL. If omitted, returns all items with the specified metadata template."
    },
    "fields": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Fields",
      "description": "By default, this endpoint returns only the most basic info about the items for which the query matches. This attribute can be used to specify a list of additional attributes to return for any item, including its metadata. This attribute takes a list of item fields, metadata template identifiers, or metadata template field identifiers. For example: * `created_by` will add the details of the user who created the item to the response. * `metadata.<scope>.<templateKey>` will return the mini-representation of the metadata instance identified by the `scope` and `templateKey`. * `metadata.<scope>.<templateKey>.<field>` will return all the mini-representation of the metadata instance identified by the `scope` and `templateKey` plus the field specified by the `field` name. Multiple fields for the same `scope` and `templateKey` can be defined. "
    },
    "marker": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Marker",
      "description": "Pagination marker from a previous response's 'next_marker' field. Use this to retrieve the next page of results when the previous response included a next_marker."
    },
    "order_by": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "object",
        "title": "QueryFilesFoldersByMetadataorderByRequest",
        "properties": {
          "direction": {
            "enum": [
              "ASC",
              "DESC",
              "asc",
              "desc"
            ],
            "type": "string",
            "title": "DirectionEnm0",
            "description": "The direction to order by, either ascending or descending. The `ordering` direction must be the same for each item in the array. "
          },
          "field_key": {
            "type": "string",
            "title": "Field Key",
            "description": "The metadata template field to order by. The `field_key` represents the `key` value of a field from the metadata template being searched for. "
          }
        },
        "description": "Request schema for `QueryFilesFoldersByMetadataorderBy`"
      },
      "title": "Order By",
      "description": "A list of template fields and directions to sort the metadata query results by. The ordering `direction` must be the same for each item in the array. "
    },
    "query_params": {
      "type": "object",
      "title": "Query Params",
      "description": "Key-value pairs for parameterized values used in the 'query' expression. Keys must match the parameter names in query (without ':'). Example: if query='status = :val', then query_params={'val': 'approved'}. Value types must match the metadata template field types (string, float, date, etc.).",
      "additionalProperties": true
    },
    "ancestor_folder_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Ancestor Folder Id",
      "description": "The folder ID to search within. Use '0' to search all folders accessible to the user. Use a specific folder ID to limit results to that folder and its subfolders. Example: '0' for root/all folders, or '12345' for a specific folder."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request schema for `QueryFilesFoldersByMetadata`"
}
```

## BOX_REFRESH_ACCESS_TOKEN
Refresh an Access Token using its client ID, secret, and refresh token. This endpoint exchanges a refresh token for a new access token. The refresh token must be valid (they expire after 60 days). Each time a refresh token is used, it is invalidated and a new one is returned along with the new access token. Access tokens expire after 1 hour and need to be refreshed periodically. Note: This action requires valid OAuth2 credentials (client_id, client_secret, and a valid refresh_token) that cannot be automatically generated.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "RefreshAccessTokenRequest",
  "required": [
    "client_id",
    "client_secret",
    "refresh_token"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "client_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Client Id",
      "description": "The client ID of the Box OAuth2 application requesting the token refresh."
    },
    "grant_type": {
      "enum": [
        "refresh_token"
      ],
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Grant Type",
      "default": "refresh_token",
      "description": "The type of OAuth2 grant being requested. Must be 'refresh_token' for this endpoint."
    },
    "client_secret": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Client Secret",
      "description": "The client secret of the Box OAuth2 application requesting the token refresh."
    },
    "refresh_token": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Refresh Token",
      "description": "The refresh token to exchange for a new access token. Each refresh token can only be used once."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request schema for `RefreshAccessToken`"
}
```

**Output schema:**

## BOX_REQUEST_ACCESS_TOKEN
Request an Access Token using either a client-side obtained OAuth 2.0 authorization code or a server-side JWT assertion. An Access Token is a string that enables Box to verify that a request belongs to an authorized session. In the normal order of operations you will begin by requesting authentication from the [authorize](#get-authorize) endpoint and Box will send you an authorization code. You will then send this code to this endpoint to exchange it for an Access Token. The returned Access Token can then be used to to make Box API calls.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "RequestAccessTokenRequest",
  "required": [
    "grant_type"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "code": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Code",
      "format": "token",
      "description": "The client-side authorization code passed to your application by Box in the browser redirect after the user has successfully granted your application permission to make API calls on their behalf. Used in combination with `authorization_code` as the `grant_type`. "
    },
    "scope": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Scope",
      "format": "space_delimited_list",
      "description": "The space-delimited list of scopes that you want apply to the new access token. The `subject_token` will need to have all of these scopes or the call will error with **401 Unauthorized**. "
    },
    "resource": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Resource",
      "format": "url",
      "description": "Full URL for the file that the token should be generated for."
    },
    "assertion": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Assertion",
      "format": "jwt",
      "description": "A JWT assertion for which to request a new access token. Used in combination with `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer` as the `grant_type`. "
    },
    "client_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Client Id",
      "description": "The Client ID of the application requesting an access token. Used in combination with `authorization_code`, `client_credentials`, or `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer` as the `grant_type`. "
    },
    "grant_type": {
      "enum": [
        "authorization_code",
        "client_credentials",
        "refresh_token",
        "urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer",
        "urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange"
      ],
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Grant Type",
      "format": "urn",
      "description": "The type of request being made, either using a client-side obtained authorization code, a refresh token, a JWT assertion, client credentials grant or another access token for the purpose of downscoping a token. "
    },
    "actor_token": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Actor Token",
      "format": "token",
      "description": "The token used to create an annotator token. This is a JWT assertion. Used in combination with `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange` as the `grant_type`. "
    },
    "client_secret": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Client Secret",
      "description": "The client secret of the application requesting an access token. Used in combination with `authorization_code`, `client_credentials`, or `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer` as the `grant_type`. "
    },
    "refresh_token": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Refresh Token",
      "format": "token",
      "description": "A refresh token used to get a new access token with. Used in combination with `refresh_token` as the `grant_type`. "
    },
    "subject_token": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Subject Token",
      "format": "token",
      "description": "The token to exchange for a downscoped token. This can be a regular access token, a JWT assertion, or an app token. Used in combination with `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange` as the `grant_type`. "
    },
    "box_subject_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Box Subject Id",
      "description": "Used in combination with `client_credentials` as the `grant_type`. Value is determined by `box_subject_type`. If `user` use user ID and if `enterprise` use enterprise ID. "
    },
    "box_shared_link": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Box Shared Link",
      "format": "url",
      "description": "Full URL of the shared link on the file or folder that the token should be generated for. "
    },
    "actor_token_type": {
      "enum": [
        "urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token"
      ],
      "type": "string",
      "title": "ActorTokenTypeEnm0",
      "format": "urn",
      "description": "The type of `actor_token` passed in. Used in combination with `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange` as the `grant_type`. "
    },
    "box_subject_type": {
      "enum": [
        "enterprise",
        "user"
      ],
      "type": "string",
      "title": "BoxSubjectTypeEnm0",
      "description": "Used in combination with `client_credentials` as the `grant_type`."
    },
    "subject_token_type": {
      "enum": [
        "urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token"
      ],
      "type": "string",
      "title": "SubjectTokenTypeEnm0",
      "description": "The type of `subject_token` passed in. Used in combination with `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange` as the `grant_type`. "
    }
  },
  "description": "Request schema for `RequestAccessToken`"
}
```

## BOX_RESEND_BOX_SIGN_REQUEST
Resends signature request emails to all outstanding signers. Use this when a signer did not receive the original email, the email was lost, or the signer accidentally deleted it. The email is sent asynchronously after the API call returns. Rate limit: Can only be called once every 10 minutes per sign request. Note: For automated reminders, consider setting 'are_reminders_enabled' to true when creating the sign request, which sends automatic reminder emails after 3, 8, 13, and 18 days. Requires Box Sign feature to be enabled and sign_requests.readwrite scope.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ResendBoxSignRequestRequest",
  "required": [
    "sign_request_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "sign_request_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Sign Request Id",
      "description": "The unique identifier (UUID) of the Box Sign request to resend. This ID can be obtained from the response when creating a sign request or by listing all sign requests using the list_box_sign_requests action."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request schema for `ResendBoxSignRequest`"
}
```

**Output schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "$defs": {
    "ResendBoxSignRequestResponse": {
      "type": "object",
      "title": "ResendBoxSignRequestResponse",
      "properties": {},
      "description": "Response schema for `ResendBoxSignRequest`\n\nReturns HTTP 202 (Accepted) with an empty body on success. The signature\nrequest emails are sent asynchronously after the API call returns.\n\nRate limit: Can only resend once every 10 minutes."
    }
  },
  "title": "ResendBoxSignRequestResponseWrapper",
```

## BOX_RESTORE_FILE
Restores a file that has been moved to the trash. An optional new parent ID can be provided to restore the file to in case the original folder has been deleted.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "RestoreFileRequest",
  "required": [
    "file_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "name": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Name",
      "description": "An optional new name for the file."
    },
    "fields": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Fields",
      "description": "A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the response. This can be used to request fields that are not normally returned in a standard response. Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the effect that none of the standard fields are returned in the response unless explicitly specified, instead only fields for the mini representation are returned, additional to the fields requested. "
    },
    "file_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "File Id",
      "description": "The unique identifier of the trashed file to restore. The file must be in the trash (deleted but not yet purged). The ID can be found by listing trashed items or from the URL in the Box web app (e.g., for `https://*.app.box.com/files/123` the file_id is `123`). Returns 404 if the file is not found in the trash."
    },
    "parent_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Parent Id",
      "description": "The ID of the parent folder to restore the file to. This is useful when the original folder has been deleted. Use '0' for the root folder."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request schema for `RestoreFile`"
}
```

**Output schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "$defs": {
    "RestoredFileData": {
      "type": "object",
      "title": "RestoredFileData",
      "properties": {
        "id": {
          "type": "string",
          "title": "Id",
          "description": "The unique identifier of the restored file."
        },
        "etag": {
          "type": "string",
          "title": "Etag",
          "description": "ETag for concurrency control."
        },
        "name": {
          "type": "string",
          "title": "Name",
          "description": "The name of the restored file."
        },
        "sha1": {
          "type": "string",
          "title": "Sha1",
          "description": "SHA1 hash of the file content."
        },
        "size": {
          "type": "integer",
          "title": "Size",
          "description": "The size of the file in bytes."
        },
        "type": {
          "type": "string",
          "title": "Type",
          "description": "Always 'file'."
        },
        "parent": {
          "type": "object",
          "title": "Parent",
          "properties": {
            "id": {
              "type": "string",
              "title": "Id",
              "description": "The unique identifier of the folder."
            },
            "etag": {
              "type": "string",
              "title": "Etag",
              "description": "ETag for concurrency control."
            },
            "name": {
              "type": "string",
              "title": "Name",
              "description": "The name of the folder."
            },
            "type": {
              "type": "string",
              "title": "Type",
              "description": "Always 'folder'."
            },
            "sequence_id": {
              "type": "string",
              "title": "Sequence Id",
              "description": "Sequence ID for concurrency control."
            }
          },
          "description": "The parent folder where the file was restored."
        },
        "owned_by": {
          "type": "object",
          "title": "Owned By",
          "properties": {
            "id": {
              "type": "string",
              "title": "Id",
              "description": "The unique identifier of the user."
            },
            "name": {
              "type": "string",
              "title": "Name",
              "description": "The display name of the user."
            },
            "type": {
              "type": "string",
              "title": "Type",
              "description": "Always 'user'."
            },
            "login": {
              "type": "string",
              "title": "Login",
              "description": "The email address of the user."
            }
          },
          "description": "The user who owns the file."
        },
        "purged_at": {
          "type": "string",
          "title": "Purged At",
          "description": "When the file would be permanently deleted (null after restore)."
        },
        "created_at": {
          "type": "string",
          "title": "Created At",
          "description": "When the file was originally created (ISO 8601)."
        },
        "created_by": {
          "type": "object",
          "title": "Created By",
          "properties": {
            "id": {
              "type": "string",
              "title": "Id",
              "description": "The unique identifier of the user."
            },
            "name": {
              "type": "string",
              "title": "Name",
              "description": "The display name of the user."
            },
            "type": {
              "type": "string",
              "title": "Type",
              "description": "Always 'user'."
            },
            "login": {
              "type": "string",
              "title": "Login",
              "description": "The email address of the user."
            }
          },
          "description": "The user who created the file."
        },
        "trashed_at": {
          "type": "string",
          "title": "Trashed At",
          "description": "When the file was moved to trash (null after restore)."
        },
        "description": {
          "type": "string",
          "title": "Description",
          "description": "The description of the file."
        },
        "item_status": {
          "type": "string",
          "title": "Item Status",
          "description": "The status of the item ('active' after successful restore)."
        },
        "modified_at": {
          "type": "string",
          "title": "Modified At",
          "description": "When the file was last modified (ISO 8601)."
        },
        "modified_by": {
          "type": "object",
          "title": "Modified By",
          "properties": {
            "id": {
              "type": "string",
              "title": "Id",
              "description": "The unique identifier of the user."
            },
            "name": {
              "type": "string",
              "title": "Name",
              "description": "The display name of the user."
            },
            "type": {
              "type": "string",
              "title": "Type",
              "description": "Always 'user'."
            },
            "login": {
              "type": "string",
              "title": "Login",
              "description": "The email address of the user."
            }
          },
          "description": "The user who last modified the file."
        },
        "sequence_id": {
          "type": "string",
          "title": "Sequence Id",
          "description": "Sequence ID for concurrency control."
        },
        "shared_link": {
          "type": "object",
          "title": "Shared Link",
          "description": "Shared link settings (if any).",
          "additionalProperties": true
        },
        "file_version": {
          "type": "object",
          "title": "File Version",
          "properties": {
            "id": {
              "type": "string",
              "title": "Id",
              "description": "The unique identifier of this file version."
            },
            "sha1": {
              "type": "string",
              "title": "Sha1",
              "description": "SHA1 hash of the file content."
            },
            "type": {
              "type": "string",
              "title": "Type",
              "description": "Always 'file_version'."
            }
          },
          "description": "The current version of the file."
        },
        "path_collection": {
          "type": "object",
          "title": "Path Collection",
          "properties": {
            "entries": {
              "type": "array",
              "items": {
                "type": "object",
                "title": "RestoredFileFolderMini",
                "properties": {
                  "id": {
                    "type": "string",
                    "title": "Id",
                    "description": "The unique identifier of the folder."
                  },
                  "etag": {
                    "type": "string",
                    "title": "Etag",
                    "description": "ETag for concurrency control."
                  },
                  "name": {
                    "type": "string",
                    "title": "Name",
                    "description": "The name of the folder."
                  },
                  "type": {
                    "type": "string",
                    "title": "Type",
                    "description": "Always 'folder'."
                  },
                  "sequence_id": {
                    "type": "string",
                    "title": "Sequence Id",
                    "description": "Sequence ID for concurrency control."
                  }
                },
                "description": "Mini representation of a folder."
              },
              "title": "Entries",
              "description": "List of folders in the path from root to parent."
            },
            "total_count": {
              "type": "integer",
              "title": "Total Count",
              "description": "Number of folders in the path."
            }
          },
          "description": "The path showing the file's location."
        },
        "content_created_at": {
          "type": "string",
          "title": "Content Created At",
          "description": "When the file content was created (ISO 8601)."
        },
        "content_modified_at": {
          "type": "string",
          "title": "Content Modified At",
          "description": "When the file content was last modified (ISO 8601)."
        }
      },
      "description": "Detailed information about the restored file."
    },
```

## BOX_RESTORE_FILE_VERSION
Restores a specific version of a file after it was deleted (trashed). This action restores a file version that was previously moved to the trash by setting its trashed_at field back to null. Do not use this endpoint to restore Box Notes - it only works with standard file formats such as PDF, DOC, PPTX, or similar. To restore a file version: 1. First use 'List all file versions' to find versions with trashed_at set 2. Then call this action with the file_id and file_version_id The restored version will have trashed_at=null and restored_at/restored_by fields populated.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "RestoreFileVersionRequest",
  "required": [
    "file_id",
    "file_version_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "file_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "File Id",
      "description": "The unique identifier that represents a file. The ID for any file can be determined by visiting a file in the web application and copying the ID from the URL. For example, for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/files/123` the `file_id` is `123`. "
    },
    "file_version_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "File Version Id",
      "description": "The ID of the file version to restore. Version IDs can be obtained by using the 'List all file versions' action with the file_id. Only versions that have been trashed (trashed_at is not null) can be restored."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request schema for `RestoreFileVersion`"
}
```

## BOX_RESTORE_FOLDER
Restores a folder that has been moved to the trash. An optional new parent ID can be provided to restore the folder to in case the original folder has been deleted. During this operation, part of the file tree will be locked, mainly the source folder and all of its descendants, as well as the destination folder. For the duration of the operation, no other move, copy, delete, or restore operation can performed on any of the locked folders.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "RestoreFolderRequest",
  "required": [
    "folder_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "name": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Name",
      "description": "An optional new name for the folder."
    },
    "fields": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Fields",
      "description": "A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the response (e.g., 'id,name,size'). This can be used to request fields that are not normally returned in a standard response. Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the effect that none of the standard fields are returned in the response unless explicitly specified, instead only fields for the mini representation are returned, additional to the fields requested. "
    },
    "folder_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Folder Id",
      "description": "The unique identifier that represent a folder. The ID for any folder can be determined by visiting this folder in the web application and copying the ID from the URL. For example, for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/folder/123` the `folder_id` is `123`. The root folder of a Box account is always represented by the ID `0`. "
    },
    "parent__id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Parent  Id",
      "description": "An optional ID of a folder to restore the folder to when the original folder no longer exists. This ID will only be used if the original folder no longer exists. Use this ID to provide a fallback location to restore the folder to if the original location has been deleted."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request schema for `RestoreFolder`"
}
```

## BOX_RESTORE_WEB_LINK
Restores a web link that has been moved to the trash. This action recovers a trashed web link and restores it to its original parent folder. If the original folder has been deleted, you can optionally specify an alternative parent folder using the parent_id parameter. You can also rename the web link during restoration using the name parameter. The web link must exist in the trash (not permanently deleted) for this action to succeed. Returns the restored web link with item_status changed from 'trashed' to 'active'.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "RestoreWebLinkRequest",
  "required": [
    "web_link_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "name": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Name",
      "description": "An optional new name for the web link. Use this to rename the web link while restoring it."
    },
    "fields": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Fields",
      "description": "A list of attributes to include in the response. Available fields include: id, type, name, url, description, created_at, modified_at, trashed_at, purged_at, item_status, created_by, modified_by, owned_by, parent, path_collection, shared_link, sequence_id, etag. If not specified, returns all standard fields. Note that specifying this parameter returns only mini representation fields plus the requested fields."
    },
    "parent_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Parent Id",
      "description": "The ID of the parent folder to restore the web link to. This is useful when the original parent folder has been deleted. If not specified, the web link will be restored to its original location. Use '0' for the root folder."
    },
    "web_link_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Web Link Id",
      "description": "The unique identifier of the trashed web link to restore. You can find trashed web link IDs by listing trashed items or using the get trashed web link action."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request schema for `RestoreWebLink`"
}
```

## BOX_SEARCH_FOR_CONTENT
Searches for files, folders, web links, and shared files across the users content or across the entire enterprise.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "SearchForContentRequest",
  "properties": {
    "sort": {
      "enum": [
        "modified_at",
        "relevance"
      ],
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Sort",
      "default": "relevance",
      "description": "Defines the order in which search results are returned. This API defaults to returning items by relevance unless this parameter is explicitly specified. * `relevance` (default) returns the results sorted by relevance to the query search term. The relevance is based on the occurrence of the search term in the items name, description, content, and additional properties. * `modified_at` returns the results ordered in descending order by date at which the item was last modified. "
    },
    "type": {
      "enum": [
        "file",
        "folder",
        "web_link"
      ],
      "type": "string",
      "title": "TypeEnm0",
      "description": "Limits the search results to any items of this type. This parameter only takes one value. By default the API returns items that match any of these types. * `file` - Limits the search results to files * `folder` - Limits the search results to folders * `web_link` - Limits the search results to web links, also known    as bookmarks "
    },
    "limit": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Limit",
      "default": 30,
      "description": "Defines the maximum number of items to return as part of a page of results. "
    },
    "query": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Query",
      "description": "The string to search for. REQUIRED unless 'mdfilters' is provided. Matched against item names, descriptions, text content, and other fields. Supports operators: \"\" (exact match), AND, OR, NOT (uppercase only)."
    },
    "scope": {
      "enum": [
        "enterprise_content",
        "user_content"
      ],
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Scope",
      "default": "user_content",
      "description": "Limits the search results to either the files that the user has access to, or to files available to the entire enterprise. The scope defaults to `user_content`, which limits the search results to content that is available to the currently authenticated user. The `enterprise_content` can be requested by an admin through our support channels. Once this scope has been enabled for a user, it will allow that use to query for content across the entire enterprise and not only the content that they have access to. "
    },
    "fields": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Fields",
      "description": "A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the response. This can be used to request fields that are not normally returned in a standard response. Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the effect that none of the standard fields are returned in the response unless explicitly specified, instead only fields for the mini representation are returned, additional to the fields requested. "
    },
    "offset": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Offset",
      "default": 0,
      "description": "The offset of the item at which to begin the response. Queries with offset parameter value exceeding 10000 will be rejected with a 400 response. "
    },
    "direction": {
      "enum": [
        "ASC",
        "DESC"
```
